message:
Merge develop into feat/per-recipient-receipt: TASK-068's signed-copy reads

Brings ADR-0090 and the session read's signed_copy / SEAL_PENDING in ahead of
the end-to-end work, so the receipt flows run against the reads they ship
beside. The backlog keeps BL-463 and BL-464; the ADR index keeps ADR-0086
and ADR-0090.

test(task-047): real flows issue each acting recipient's receipt and both routes serve it

Three acceptance flows through the signer's routes and the relay: a
SEQUENTIAL_PADES envelope with two signers and an approver, a SINGLE_SEAL
signer who gets 409 RECEIPT_NOT_READY until the relay runs, and a decliner
whose receipt the integrator downloads. Also covers two signers of one step
each getting a receipt naming their own revision, and records the tests in ADR-0086.

fix(task-069): a pending field owner holds a document's early seal

A recipient who owns a field on a document records its value at their commit,
and the document's next revision draws it, so the early seal now waits for
them and their landing requests it. Adds the cross-tenant 404 test on the
sealed route and brings the docs in line with the new rule.

test(task-047): pin the receipt registry policies and the trail goldens' AC-15

Also corrects the docs: every list of the session credential's routes now
names the decline and the receipt, and RECEIPT_NOT_READY lifts only once the
receipt is issued, not by itself.

docs(adr): accept ADR-0087, a document is sealed once it is final

Accepted by the owner on 2026-10-23; it amends ADR-0073 §2.5, ADR-0039 §10 and
ADR-0072 §2.2. The handoff and domain models say the same, and new tests
kill the mutants left on the early seal's changed lines.

docs(task-047): name the receipt beside the trail in shared comments

Renderer, custodian and build comments now mention the receipt as well as
the trail, RECEIPT_NOT_READY's published detail promises no time, and the
session credential's docblocks point at the route declarations. Also makes
the storage lifecycle scenario pick the superseded copy by its container.

docs(task-069): describe the decline's seal request as finding nothing today

No decline secures the agreement yet, so admitDecline() requests seals that
find nothing; the early-seal docblocks now say who runs the handler.
style(storage): import the array functions the lifecycle scenario calls

feat(task-070): the copy list says where the recipient's own copy stands

GET /api/v1/copy now answers signed_copy beside documents, with the same
rule as the session read: null means no act of theirs, and a decliner reads
null before and after the end. The docs follow ADR-0090 after an admitted commit.

test(task-047): pin the receipt's controllers, gathering and assembly

Infection on the branch's changed lines found these unguarded, so the
controllers, the gatherer and the assembler get tests where their fixtures
no longer always agree. The receipt is also documented in the schema, the
domain models and the frontend handoffs.

test(task-047): pin the receipt issuance, conservation, registry and routes

Covers the read-back search and lost-claim cause, the conservation job's
receipt loop across tenants, the registry's unconserved read and id refusal,
and the receipt routes' published callers, codes and PDF.

docs(task-047): accept ADR-0086

Accepted by the owner on 2026-10-26 after TASK-047 exercised every section.
Also pins the receipt dry run across row orders and keeps Infection from
mutating OpenAPI arguments the spec test already pins.

Merge feat/per-recipient-receipt: TASK-047, each recipient who acts gets a sealed receipt

A signer, approver or decliner gets a PDF/A-3a receipt, sealed through
PdfSealer, that attests their own act and nothing about the other parties.

Merge develop into feat/copy-link: TASK-047's sealed receipt

One docs-only conflict: the ADR index, graph and crosswalk keep the ADR-0086
and ADR-0088 rows in id order.

Merge develop into feat/early-document-seal: TASK-047

Brings the per-recipient sealed receipt (ADR-0086). The only conflict was the
ADR index, where both rows are kept.

feat(task-070): a copy read credential reads its recipient's receipt

GET /api/v1/copy/receipt serves the recipient's sealed receipt under the
copy read credential, through the same rule as the session receipt route.

feat(task-070): the copy list says whether a receipt is owed

GET /api/v1/copy gains has_receipt once the recipient's own act closed their
signing session, read without taking a lock and covering approvers too. Two
end-to-end scenarios walk the whole copy, and the docs name the receipt route.

Merge feat/early-document-seal: TASK-069, a document is sealed as soon as it is final

Under SEQUENTIAL_PADES a document with a signature is sealed by its own early
seal once the agreement is secured and nobody can still sign it or fill a field.
Merge develop into feat/recipient-notices: TASK-047, TASK-068 and TASK-069

Merge develop into feat/copy-link: TASK-069's early document seal

One docs-only conflict: the ADR index, graph and crosswalk keep the ADR-0087
and ADR-0088 rows in id order.

feat(notification): keep one locked part-notice record per recipient

Notification gets notification.recipient_part_notice, one row per envelope
and recipient (ADR-0089 §2.3). The owner also chose that signed_copy reads
FINAL once every document a recipient can see is sealed, early seal included,
and that a decline requests the seal of what it made final.

test(task-070): the copy list refuses a request missing its credential attributes

Also rewrites the prose the copy link made false so it names the copy link,
the copy list and the receipt, and fixes the remaining comments saying a
recipient's self-serve copy does not exist.

docs(task-070): mark every amendment by ADR-0088 as Proposed

Dated notes on ADR-0045 and the others say ADR-0088 is Proposed and that its
acceptance is the owner's. The Signing Session model, the architecture map
and the task record name the copy surface, with its status and deferrals.

feat(notification): add the recipient's act, part-complete and decline notices

Three new NotificationPurpose cases for a recipient's own part, with their
copy. Evidence & Audit also records its first event: issuing a receipt
records RECEIPT_ISSUED inside its claim.

feat(task-071): a recipient's part ends with a recorded fact

Landing and an admitted decline now record RECIPIENT_PART_ENDED, and a
decline requests the seal of the documents it made final. Part-notice
fixtures pin the database clock, and the docs say a decline requests seals.

feat(notification): each ending notice has a signer's twin about their sealed documents

Under ADR-0089 §2.4 a recipient who signed an envelope that ended without
agreement is told, after the seal, that their documents are sealed. Tests
show a trail and a receipt still build over a stream holding the new facts,
and that the history route serves the new purposes.

feat(session): signed_copy reads FINAL once every document the recipient sees is sealed

Under SEQUENTIAL_PADES a recipient whose own act landed reads FINAL when
nothing is withheld from them and all their documents are sealed. A new
PartNoticePolicy decides which part notice a recipient is owed, and tests
census every admitted act and envelope outcome.

test(task-070): pin the copy gate's records, use cases and refusals

Infection left mutants alive on the copy access record and the three copy
gate use cases; these tests assert the intervals and refusals they changed.

test(task-070): pin each copy controller's answer and published contract

The diff-scoped Infection run credits only tests that name a changed class,
so each controller now has a unit test of its answer and its OpenAPI contract.
test(task-070): pin the copy reads, the record's store and the credential parse

feat(notification): a recipient's part and their receipt reach Notification

RecipientPartEnded and ReceiptIssued each dispatch a command whose use case
reads the envelope once and sends the notice the part-notice policy owes.

feat(notification): an early document seal re-decides every recipient's part notice

A part that was not final when it ended becomes complete once the last
document the recipient can see is sealed. A signer or decliner is no longer
sent the linkless ending notice at the close, and a repeated request leaves
the first occasion untouched.

fix(event-log): the relay walks transaction ids in numeric order across a power of ten

relayBatch() and drainPreviousEpoch() ordered by the text alias of the
transaction id while the cursor compared it as a number, so a batch crossing
a power of ten could lose a fact.

Merge fix/relay-orders-by-transaction-id: the relay walks transaction ids in numeric order

Both relay reads ordered by the text alias of the transaction id while the
cursor compared it as a number; they now order numerically, so no fact is lost.

Merge fix/relay-orders-by-transaction-id into feat/copy-link

Brings the relay ordering fix (BL-406) that made EventRelayEpochResetTest fail
in every full run of this branch.

feat(notification): at the end, close each recipient's part-notice record separately

The end is the safety net of ADR-0089 §2.3. NotifyCompletedEnvelopeRecipients
now owns its unit of work and draws one boundary per recipient, so one
failure no longer blocks the others.

test(notification): one recipient's failed end leaves the others committed

The per-recipient boundary was only tested with doubles that roll nothing
back; this runs it on the real unit of work.

docs(task-070): accept ADR-0088

Accepted by the owner on 2026-10-26 with TASK-070's criteria green.

Merge feat/copy-link: TASK-070, a recipient reads their copy through a read-only link

An opaque, digest-stored copy link opens a recipient's documents and sealed
receipt, passing the declared access gate again on a copy access record of
its own. A 15-minute read credential admits no act. ADR-0088 accepted.

Merge develop into feat/recipient-notices: TASK-070 (copy link) and the relay ordering fix

Conflicts were in nelmio_api_doc.yaml, the ADR index and the notification
application code.

feat(notification): every part notice carries the recipient's copy link

RecipientNotices mints the link through Session's guarded CopyLinkIssuer
when the notice is created, and the nine link-bearing notices show it as a
button and in the SMS. The docs say FINAL comes once every visible document
is sealed.

feat(notification): the copy-ready notice carries the member's copy link

SEALED_COPY_READY keeps its timing and audience under ADR-0073 §2.15 but its
link is now the recipient's copy link, and it reaches delegated members too.
The end owes a link-bearing notice only to a recipient the mint admits, and
a refused mint fails only that recipient's boundary.

test(task-071): end-to-end notices for a decline and for early-sealed documents

Over HTTP, the relay and the real signer: a decline tells the decliner once,
the signer after the seal and the silent recipient at the close; a carrier
whose documents are sealed early is told while the waybill is open.

feat(messenger): Evidence & Audit's facts reach the queue Notification reads

RECEIPT_ISSUED is Evidence & Audit's first event and Notification reacts to
it, so async_events now routes it to Notification's queue. End-to-end tests
cover the waybill and a single-seal envelope, each reading only its own mail.

fix(notification): a part-notice decision reads the envelope after its row lock

Also makes a document seal wait on a part still being written, labels the
receipt and part-ended facts in the audit trail, and completes the published
copy-link list.

docs(task-071): the part-notice record, its facts and the copy link are in the models

Domain models, handoffs and amended ADRs now state the part-notice record.
Comments on the seal command and the copy-ready rule are corrected, and new
tests assert the notice variables, the end of a part and the receipt fact.

docs(task-071): accept ADR-0089

Accepted by the owner once TASK-071's verification bars were green. Also pins
that a single-seal part is not final even when its document is sealed.

Merge feat/recipient-notices: TASK-071, a recipient is told when their part ends

Each recipient hears at their own act, when every document they can see is
sealed, and at the end, with at most one notice of each kind. Every notice
carries the recipient's read-only copy link. ADR-0089 accepted.

feat(task-072): the copy and session reads publish what the recipient did

The signer's redesigned screens need when and how the recipient acted and
whether their receipt is issued. The copy open, gate and receipt answers are
no-store, each document reader gains readAll(), and ext-zip is now a declared
platform requirement.

docs(task-073): the integrator may name an envelope's sender

An optional sender (display name, tax id) declared at creation by a tenant an
operator enabled, shown to recipients.

feat(task-072): read a recipient's own act, notified destinations and receipt standing

OwnAct gives the act and its admitted instant in one rule, NotifiedDestination
lists one masked contact per declared channel, and ReceiptStandingReader lets
Evidence & Audit publish ISSUED, PENDING or nothing through a contract port.

feat(task-072): bundle documents as a ZIP whose entry names cannot escape or collide

BundleEntryNames strips control characters and path separators and falls back
to document.pdf for a hollow name. Comments on the document reader and OwnAct
are corrected.

feat(task-072): the session read model carries the recipient's act and receipt standing

SigningSessionReader asks ReceiptStandingReader only after every refusal. The
receipt routes now decide through the same standing rule, and the bundle's
temporary file is removed when the archive cannot be built.

feat(task-072): a recipient downloads all their documents as one ZIP

GET /api/v1/signing/session/documents.zip and GET /api/v1/copy/documents.zip.
GET /api/v1/signing/session now also emits acted_at, receipt and notified_on,
and the route census classifies the bundle as a read.

feat(task-072): the copy list carries the recipient's act, receipt standing and outcome

GET /api/v1/copy now answers acted_at, act, receipt, envelope_outcome and
recipient_name beside its existing keys, is not stored, and reads the receipt
standing from Evidence & Audit. Tests keep the session read and the copy list
in agreement on when the recipient acted.

test(task-072): the card reads PENDING then ISSUED end to end

ADR-0091 lands as Proposed and the prose that said Session never reads
Evidence & Audit is corrected. The bundle waits for the copy, and every copy
route is covered.

Merge develop: TASK-073's record and ADR-0092 Proposed, beside ADR-0091

docs/adr/README.md keeps both decisions' index rows, graph edges and
crosswalk rows, ADR-0091 before ADR-0092.

feat(task-072): bundle entry names carry no format character or reserved name

BundleEntryNames strips Cf/Zl/Zp as well as Cc, composes to NFC before the
duplicate check and avoids Windows reserved names. Both document readers name
every servable document before a byte is read, and a minted copy link is
answered with Cache-Control no-store.

feat(task-072): both bundle routes stream an archive built on disk

DocumentArchive writes each entry to its own temporary file, one document in
memory at a time, and leaves no file behind, even when close() fails. An entry
name gets .pdf when it has no extension.

refactor(session): the readers and the archive no longer hold a whole bundle in memory

The bundle now holds at most two documents at a time. The docs state the
memory behaviour, the reserved names and the .pdf rule as the code has them,
and the models say what the copy card reads.

docs(task-072): accept ADR-0091

Accepted by the owner on 2026-10-27 once its section 5 tests and the
architecture check were green. Also adds tests for the bundle's names,
archive and response where Infection found them open, and fixes the ADR-0088
row in the domain-model index.

Merge feat/copy-card-reads: TASK-072, the copy card reads what the recipient did

GET /api/v1/signing/session gains acted_at, receipt and notified_on, and
GET /api/v1/copy gains acted_at, act, receipt, envelope_outcome and
recipient_name.

feat(task-075): Evidence & Audit answers a recipient's own receipt through a contract port

RecipientReceiptReader is the port Session's documents bundles will read the
receipt through. The record asks for a with_receipt parameter on both
documents.zip routes.

fix(signature-execution): the form engine takes and returns the PDF as raw bytes

The adapter and the pyHanko script now share one framing: a line of JSON
naming the PDF length, then the raw bytes. Tests cover the script on its own,
a 32 MiB PDF byte-exact within a memory limit, a body starting with a newline,
and a response arriving in pieces.

refactor(task-075): the two receipt routes answer through RecipientReceiptRule

The session and copy handlers hold no refusals of their own. Session also
gains RecipientBundle, which runs both bundle routes in a fixed order and
refuses the whole bundle when the receipt refuses.

feat(task-075): both bundle routes take with_receipt=1

The bundle ends with the recipient's own receipt, and a substituted receipt
is logged. The OpenAPI descriptions document the parameter and every code,
and nine acceptance cases run on the live stack.

docs(task-074): no prose describes the base64 framing any more

BL-455 no longer says PHP holds the PDF three times. Also tests that the
adapter reads a response arriving in pieces beside stderr.

test(task-075): each recipient's bundle carries their own receipt and nobody else's

The handoff, the amended ADRs and the domain models say a bundle can carry
the receipt, and the signing bundle's published 404 also covers a recipient
with no receipt.
docs(task-075): ADR-0091 says its receipt handlers decide through RecipientReceiptRule

Merge fix/form-engine-binary-framing: TASK-074, the form engine speaks raw bytes

A large document no longer times out or gets the worker killed for memory on
its way to pyHanko.
Merge develop: TASK-074's form engine wire

test(task-075): measure coverage of every class named Bundle

phpunit.dist.xml excluded every file ending in Bundle.php from coverage, a
leftover meant for framework bundles. Also pins the receipt refusals by
message, accepts ADR-0093 (owner, 2026-10-28), and adds a copy bundle test
for a reader that lists no document.

Merge feat/bundle-with-receipt: TASK-075, a bundle can carry the recipient's receipt

Both documents.zip routes take with_receipt=1 and then end with the
recipient's sealed receipt, refused whole when the receipt is not ready.

fix(trail): the geolocation limitation applies only while no party reported a position

The trail stated that no party's geographic location is captured whenever a
party opened its session or acted, even when one had reported a position.
Merge fix/trail-geolocation-limitation: say no location was captured only when none was

fix(evidence-audit): the JSON embedded in a trail or receipt follows its PDF's name

A new trail attaches <envelope>.json and a receipt <envelope>.<recipient>.json
in lower case. TrailFileName::of() builds the trail's name for the route and
for the seal.

feat(receipt): a receipt is named <envelope>.<recipient>.pdf in one place

ReceiptFileName::of() builds the name, used by the route and by the seal. The
documents bundle is named <envelope>.zip and carries the receipt under its
route's name; the docs and a handoff say downloads are named by envelope.

Merge fix/download-names: TASK-076, downloaded files are named by their envelope

The bundle, audit-trail and receipt routes name their files <envelope>.zip,
<envelope>.pdf and <envelope>.<recipient>.pdf.

feat(receipt): lead with how the act ended and keep the technical detail in an annex

The page opens with a band stating the act, its time and who acted. The
personal group lists each one-time code's masked contact and the signature
image's digest, and tests read the band, local times and header.

feat(receipt): the body keeps one device line and the technical detail moves to the annex

The annex no longer prints the recipient's step, the footer drops the
recipient id. Tests tell a receipt's codes from the other recipient's by what
was sent and pin the band's role beside the name.

feat(evidence-audit): the receipt prints each code's masked contact and the image digest

The recipient section lists the contact each one-time code was sent to, and
the signature image digest with its caption. The published form is pinned to
its schema, UTC times and closed key set; ADR-0086 and the models name them.

refactor(evidence-audit): name the receipt act's digest field as its published key

Also tests that a decliner's masked phone is printed and the full number is
not, and records in ADR-0086 what pins it.

Merge feat/receipt-redesign: TASK-077, the receipt leads with how the act ended

The receipt opens with a status band, prints peninsular local time, repeats a
header from page 2 and keeps its technical detail in an annex.

docs(key-management): describe the keyrings and add their schema and config

Key Management is a new module in its own schema. The decline reason is
encrypted under keyrings that can be erased (ADR-0096), so this part carries
the docs, migration and config that describe and set it up.
feat(key-management): add the contracts the decline reason crosses
feat(key-management): add the keyring domain and its ciphers
feat(session): encrypt the decline reason through the keyrings
feat(key-management): add the adapters for keyrings, wrapping keys and storage
test(key-management): cover the decline reason across envelope, audit and identity
test(key-management): cover the application use cases
test(key-management): cover the keyrings against a real database
test(key-management): add the fakes for the keyring ports
test(key-management): unit-test the keyring domain and ciphers

test(key-management): cover the decline flow, event payloads and the rest

Final part of the Key Management change: Session acceptance, application,
integration and unit tests, the SignatureExecution integration test and the
event-payload fixtures. The decline reason is encrypted in the log and no
column is; the full suite passes.

docs(key-management): the docs say the log's decline reason is encrypted, no column is

The architecture overview did not name Key Management, and the pointers on
recipient.decline_reason still sent readers to the old description.

test(persistence): stop DBAL profiling in the test kernel

The test kernel keeps no query after it runs, so peak memory in a full run
no longer grows with the row count.

test(notification): order a re-invitation after the send

The channel change now comes after the send, so the two invitations no longer
tie on requested_at.

test(notification): assert on the provider's whole code in the history

The history route's test no longer fails when a random id contains 550.

docs(event-log): encrypt the log's other free text, with its schema, config and domain

ENVELOPE_CREATED.title, DOCUMENT_ADDED_TO_ENVELOPE.name, ENVELOPE_VOIDED.reason
and SIGNATURE_COMMITTED.reservations hold an encrypted value, as
SESSION_DECLINED.reason does. The log encrypts each pending text at the append;
facts written earlier keep their text in clear and still decode.

feat(event-log): encrypt the other free text at the append, in application and adapters

Creating an envelope, adding a document, voiding with a reason and committing
with reservations now need the registered wrapping key. The trail and the
receipt decrypt in the worker, and a process builds the key services only for
a pending text.
